title: ModSecurity v3 object materialization uses a predictable archive path outside its private staging boundary
title_de: ModSecurity-v3-Objektmaterialisierung verwendet einen vorhersagbaren Archivpfad außerhalb ihrer privaten Staging-Grenze
protocol: Git object archive materialization and filesystem destination containment
profile: Parent PR #55 runtime-evidence remediation, isolated Framework candidate based on 784977615acfc55567e37b863309abc4a38ac877
technical_claim: The candidate computes $parent/.modsecurity-v3-archive-$$.tar, checks that pathname, and later passes it to git archive --output. A concurrent actor able to create entries in the materialization parent can replace that predictable pathname with a symlink after the check, redirecting archive creation outside the intended snapshot boundary.
entry_point: Direct, Apache, and NGINX Framework ModSecurity v3 consumers call ci_materialize_approved_modsecurity_v3_source, which calls ci_modsecurity_v3_materialize_git_tree for the root and each approved child.
source_to_sink_or_broken_control: The controlled destination parent contributes a pathname entry after the helper's -e/-L check. The helper invokes ci_modsecurity_v3_git archive --output=<predictable path>, and Git follows the substituted symlink to write the generated archive at the attacker-selected target before tar reads it.
attacker_prerequisites: Ability to race directory-entry creation in the parent of a configured ModSecurity v3 snapshot destination.
A build path that invokes the object-materialization helper with that destination parent.
observed_behavior: A task-owned real-Git regression created a symlink for the legacy predictable archive pathname between the helper's check and Git archive invocation. The helper returned 0, while the regression observed that the archive was created at the controlled outside target.
expected_behavior: Archive and extraction intermediates must be created only in an atomically allocated private staging directory. A predictable entry in the destination parent must neither redirect Git output nor cause a write outside the intended materialization boundary.
impact: A concurrent actor sharing the destination parent can redirect a Git archive write to another filesystem target writable by the Framework/CI identity. The defect is a high-impact path-containment violation in a supply-chain build-input boundary. The controlled proof used only benign temporary files and never executed modified source bytes.
preconditions: The materialization destination parent is shared or otherwise writable by the competing actor.
The actor can create the predictable archive pathname after the helper's preflight check and before git archive opens it.
reproduction: Create a task-owned local Git repository with a committed benign build.sh.

Invoke ci_modsecurity_v3_materialize_git_tree through a temporary Git wrapper that creates symlinks for the legacy .modsecurity-v3-archive-<candidate-pid>.tar pathname in the configured destination parent.
Observe that the pre-remediation helper returns 0 and the benign outside archive target exists, proving that git archive followed the replacement symlink.

evidence.summary: The failing real-Git regression showed that the helper returned 0 while a generated archive appeared at the controlled outside target through a replaced predictable archive pathname.

evidence.command: RTK-wrapped focused provenance suite, public-parent/empty-placeholder control, Framework Make provenance contract, documentation checks, and full Framework lint
evidence.summary: Post-fix local controls passed: no predictable archive parent path, private-parent rejection before empty-placeholder removal, no .git metadata in object snapshots, full lint, and independent review without a remaining high or critical cross-UID blocker.

root_cause: The helper validates pathnames before use but reserves neither the archive file nor an immutable private staging directory. Its $$/name is predictable, and tar also consumes the destination pathname after a separate validation step.
proposed_remediation: The local candidate now requires the destination parent to be private before any destination mutation, creates an atomically allocated private staging directory with restrictive permissions, writes the Git archive and extraction tree only inside that directory, and publishes only the completed tree to a previously absent destination. It rejects normal/symlink/pre-existing destinations except the explicit empty Gitlink placeholder and preserves the residual same-UID filesystem-race limitation of portable path-based shell code.
acceptance_criteria: The archive-path replacement regression passes: the controlled outside target remains absent and the legitimate committed snapshot is present at the destination.
The helper uses an atomically allocated private staging directory and no predictable archive filename in the caller-controlled parent.
A destination symlink or pre-existing destination fails closed before a build action.
Direct, Apache, and NGINX legitimate object-materialization controls remain successful with no Git metadata in their snapshot.
Focused security regressions, the complete provenance suite, syntax, Make, documentation, Change Record, lint, retained-source checks, and independent bypass review pass before Framework delivery.
validation_plan: Run the original archive-path replacement regression after remediation and confirm the outside target is absent.
Run a legitimate real-Git snapshot control and the direct fake consumer control.
Review destination symlink, pre-existing destination, private-stage cleanup, parent replacement, and same-UID race limitations.
Run the complete Framework ModSecurity v3 provenance suite and selected Framework documentation/lint checks.
legitimate_control_tests: A temporary local Git source materializes its committed build.sh into the requested destination while the controlled outside archive target remains absent.
The clean exact approved root plus eight initialized pinned children materializes through the direct Framework consumer without submodule mutation.
bypass_review: Review predictable archive names, archive-file symlinks, destination symlinks, parent replacement, extraction destination replacement, publication race behavior, restrictive staging permissions, root/child snapshot coverage, Git metadata exclusion, and the residual same-UID filesystem attacker model.
deduplication_note: Not a duplicate of FND-FRAMEWORK-0034. FND-FRAMEWORK-0034 owns hidden mutable source bytes and the validation-to-copy source boundary. This finding owns an independently remediable archive/extraction destination-path containment race after object-based materialization was introduced.
evidence_limitations: The proof creates only a benign archive below a task-owned temporary directory and never writes outside that fixture.

The reproducer models a competing actor able to create directory entries in the materialization parent; it does not claim protection against a same-UID actor with arbitrary process or private-stage access.
residual_risk: The cross-UID archive/path-containment boundary is fixed locally. Portable path-based shell controls cannot isolate a concurrent same-UID writer, so that limitation remains documented. A separate Framework PR, exact-head checks/review/Sonar evidence, Framework-master verification, and a separately authorized Parent gitlink update remain required before this finding can become verified or unblock Parent PR #55 runtime evidence. No Framework master, Parent gitlink, or MRTS action has occurred.

history.detail: A focused real-Git regression replaced the predictable archive pathname after the helper's check. The helper returned 0 and the archive was created at the controlled outside target.

The finding is distinct from source-byte integrity because it concerns output-path containment after immutable Git-object selection. It is P0/high/validated, in_progress, and blocks Framework delivery and Parent PR #55 runtime evidence until fixed and verified.

The candidate uses a private random stage and validates the parent before any destination mutation. Archive-race, public-parent, normal/symlink destination, empty Gitlink-placeholder, snapshot, Make, lint, documentation, and independent-review controls passed. Status is fixed, not verified, because no Framework PR or master verification exists.
